updates.scope_and_remaining_work: Complete at the finite-dimensional algebraically closed scope inherited from the single-operator theorem. The actual intrinsic multiplicity for X-C(a) is identified with the dimension of the actual eigenspace, without diagonalizability. The canonical natural and cardinal seed ranks equal the maximum over the actual spectrum. Off-spectrum dimensions are zero, the empty-spectrum/zero-space maximum is defined as zero, and the spectral maximum is attained on nonzero spaces. No executable spectral algorithm is claimed.

The arbitrary-field cyclic/minpoly bridge, intrinsic primary multiplicities, primary label injectivity and conditional invariant-factor count remain proved. Block 05 adds an actual polynomial-module equivalence between a cyclic operator module and k[X]/(minpoly(T)), and proves both cyclicity and minpoly=charpoly equivalent to one-dimensional eigenspaces at every spectral value when the ORIGINAL field is already algebraically closed. Remaining for the printed six-way statement: formal scalar extension to an algebraic closure with preservation/descent of cyclicity or minimal polynomial, and exact assembly of the intrinsic-primary/rational-canonical clauses. A theorem native to an algebraically closed field is not silently treated as the scalar-extension clause for an arbitrary base field. No executable canonical-form construction is asserted.
